text:
jia: FYI running quant bring-up for Eos9B (Gemma fork) in int4 and seeing a consistent drop in ROUGE/QA on long-context prompts, looks like something with rotary handshake + vocab boundaries.

sam: Can you paste the eval numbers and the exact quant command?

jia: Sure — baseline fp16 -> rougeL: 42.1, qa-f1: 68.3. After int4 conversion rougeL: 36.8, qa-f1: 62.0. Repro on local and on dedicated. Command: ```python convert.py --model eos9b.fp16 --out eos9b.int4 --quant-method gptq --group-size 128 --per-channel```

olga: Do we see token repetition or weird BOS/EOS behavior? That often hints at vocab id offsets.

jia: Yeah, noticed repeated tokens around token ids > 50200 in long contexts. Short prompts are mostly fine. Also saw small but systematic phase drift in runtime logs: `rotary_scale_layer_9: 0.9987 expected 1.0` across runs.

ben: Hmm. Could be rotary param mismatch between our loader and the exported Gemma weights (some forks use headwise vs global scale). Which rotary implementation did convert.py assume?

jia: convert.py currently assumes 'per_head' rotary scaling (legacy Gemma behaviour). Upstream Eos9B repo used 'shared_scale' in their latest release. I missed that in the metadata.

sam: That would produce subtle head-phase misalignments, especially with quant noise, and could amplify at long context. Try re-exporting with the other rotary mode. Also check tokenizer vocab offsets — some Gemma forks add sentinel tokens at the end.

jia: Re-ran with `--rotary-mode shared_scale` and re-quantized: intermediate evals look much better: rougeL 41.0, qa-f1 67.1 (still slightly down but much closer).

ci-bot: nightly-evals/6527778888: run finished — baseline: rougeL=42.1, int4(shared_rotary)=41.0, int4(per_head)=36.8.

olga: Nice, that points at the rotary handshake being the primary culprit. The vocab shadowing could still cause tail issues. Can you dump token ids for a failing transcript?

jia: Pasted a small extract: ```tokens: [50198, 50199, 50200, 50201, 50202] -> decoded: ["<unk>", "the", "\u200b", "the", "the"]``` Notable: 50200 decodes to zero-width joiner in our tokenizer mapping — suspect post-processing remap broke because quant converter renumbered special tokens.

ben: Oof. Two independent issues: rotary-mode mismatch + special token remap. The converter probably assumes original tokenizer.json order. Did you use the v2 tokenizer from the upstream repo?

jia: I used the packaged tokenizer from the model archive (which has extra sentinels). convert.py does a naive `vocab_size = len(tokens)` check and then slices rotary tables by head_dim*vocab_size which caused mis-indexing.

sam: Short-term mitigation: add explicit tokenizer path to convert step and verify token id table equality. Long-term: update convert.py to read `token_id_map.json` and do safe remap logic. Also add a rotary-mode autodetect that runs a quick head-phase check (see ben's script).

ben: I have a tiny probe script that compares rotary cos/sin consistency across heads; runs in ~5s per model. Use `--rotary-probe` during onboarding. Paste below: ```python
# probe snippet
import torch
m = load_model("eos9b.fp16")
probe = get_rotary_params(m, layer=0)
# compute headwise L2 between expected shared vs per_head
print((probe['per_head'] - probe['shared']).abs().mean())
```

olga: Good. Also add a unit test: quantize small slice and run sentinel decoding smoke test (check that decoded tokens for ids > (vocab_size - 10) match upstream).

jiа: (typo) jia: Will implement both patches. Initial plan: 1) force re-export with shared_scale to validate, 2) add `--tokenizer-file` arg and safe remap logic, 3) rotary-probe CI step.

sam: Sounds right. Can one of you do a short PR for convert.py with tests? I'll review.

ben: I'll open the PR and include the probe and a small test vector from the Eos9B archive.

ci-bot: pr/3142 opened by ben: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-tools/pull/3142 — includes rotary autodetect + tokenizer remap and unit tests.

jia: Re-ran full eval with PR applied; int4 now matches much closer: rougeL 41.6, qa-f1 67.7. Long-context hallucination rate down ~55%. Great catch everyone :tada:

olga: Awesome. Follow-up: let's add an onboarding checklist item: "rotary mode / tokenizer remap verified" for all Gemma and Mistral forks.

sam: Agreed. I'll add to the model-onboarding playbook.

ben: Leaving notes in the PR for future models (Qwen/LLama variants) — some Qwen exports had similar extra sentinel behavior.

jia: Thanks team, closing the loop here. If any regressions show up I'll reopen.
